title: I gave Claude Fable 5.2 one prompt and got a playable 3D stealth shooter: 3 missions, no engine, no art assets (trailer + source)
author: Admirable_Fondant731
selftext:
The prompt was roughly: "create an immersive futuristic stealth game, war, robots, AI theme. Impress me." No spec, no follow-up design notes.

What came back is a browser game in about 3,000 lines of JavaScript on Three.js:

\* 3 missions: an arctic night infiltration, a burning city with a shielded walker boss, and an assault on a rogue AI's citadel with a timed escape  
\* Stealth that actually works: line of sight, noise, crouching, patrols that investigate, cameras, alarms that call reinforcements  
\* Enemies path around buildings with A\\\* on a nav grid it built itself  
\* 4 weapons, grenades, a cloak, night vision, radar, tactical map  
\* Zero asset files. Every model, texture and sound effect is generated in code

Being honest about the limits: it's stylised low-poly, not realistic, and the balance is untuned because nobody has playtested it properly yet. The game itself was the one prompt. The trailer, the repo and the trailer's voice and music (ElevenLabs) were follow-up requests.

The trailer is real gameplay, but driven by scripted input, so the aim is steadier than a human's.

Source, MIT-licensed Three.js vendored, runs with \`python3 run.py\`: \[https://github.com/dantecomedia/null-horizon\](https://github.com/dantecomedia/null-horizon)

Happy to answer questions about the prompt or how it structured the code.
